title: Modi Inaugurates Pune Metro Pink Line, Launches Rs 21,800 Crore Expansion
excerpt: The 23-kilometre Pink Line linking Hinjewadi's IT hub with Shivajinagar opens to passengers on November 4, while foundation stones were laid for four Phase-II corridors estimated at Rs 13,500 crore.
body:
• Passenger services on Pune Metro's 23-kilometre Pink Line start on November 4, initially covering 17 of its 23 stations, according to coverage of the inauguration.
  • The Pink Line, built at a cost of more than Rs 8,300 crore, runs from Maan to District Court station and links the Hinjewadi IT hub with Shivajinagar.
  • Prime Minister Narendra Modi also laid the foundation stone for Phase-II — Lines 2A, 2B, 4 and 4A — estimated at around Rs 13,500 crore, taking the combined package to around Rs 21,800 crore.
  • The line will be operated entirely by women train operators, and around 30 per cent of its electricity needs are envisaged to be met through solar power.

PUNE — Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday inaugurated Pune Metro Line 3, known as the Pink Line, and laid the foundation stone for four Phase-II corridors through video conferencing. Together, the projects are worth around Rs 21,800 crore, according to coverage of the inauguration.

The distinction matters for commuters. The Pink Line is the corridor that is opening. The other four lines are the planned expansion whose foundation stone was laid at the same programme, as the Prime Minister's Office outlined ahead of the event in material summarised by ISR Grajan's report on the PMO announcement.

A direct link between Hinjewadi and Shivajinagar

The Pink Line runs approximately 23 kilometres from Maan to District Court Metro station. The Pune Metropolitan Region Development Authority, which undertook the project, describes it as an elevated corridor measuring 23.203 kilometres with 23 stations, at a cost including land acquisition and shifting of utilities of Rs 8,313 crore.

https://x.com/narendramodi/status/2117243062640316644

That route connects Hinjewadi, one of Pune's largest technology and employment hubs, with Shivajinagar, a major administrative, commercial and transport centre. Integration at the District Court interchange connects the new line with the existing Metro network.

Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said at the programme that thousands of people commute to Hinjewadi every day and often spend one to two hours in traffic congestion, according to ANI coverage published by APNA MA TV. Fadnavis said a total of 120 kilometres of Metro lines in Pune had either been completed or were under construction.

"A better-connected Pune is a faster-growing Pune! New Metro projects will boost the city's growth and improve Ease of Living"

— Narendra Modi, Prime Minister

Women operators and solar power

The entire Pink Line will be operated by women train operators, the Prime Minister's Office said. Around 30 per cent of the line's total electricity requirements are envisaged to be met through solar power. Fadnavis made the same green point at the programme, saying the corridor would generate 30 per cent of its energy requirements on its own.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DfPaHilk3ZW/

The project was awarded to a joint venture of TRIL Urban Transport Pvt Ltd and Siemens Project Ventures GmbH, with a dedicated project company, Pune IT City Metro Rail Limited, established to carry it out, PMRDA said. The authority describes the arrangement as a public-private partnership under the central government's New Metro Rail Policy, 2017, on a Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer model.

What Phase-II adds

Phase-II comprises Lines 2A, 2B, 4 and 4A, at an estimated cost of around Rs 13,500 crore. Lines 2A and 2B will together cover approximately 12.75 kilometres. Line 2A will connect Vanaz with Chandani Chowk, while Line 2B will extend from Ramwadi to Vitthalwadi.

Line 4 will run 25.52 kilometres from Kharadi to Khadakwasla, and Line 4A will cover 6.12 kilometres from Nal Stop to Manik Baug. The corridors are intended to bring areas including Kharadi, Magarpatta, Hadapsar, Swargate, Manik Baug, Nanded City, Pune Cantonment and Warje within the expanded network.

Interchange facilities at Swargate, Nal Stop and Kharadi Bypass are intended to connect the new corridors with the existing Metro network and intercity bus services, the PMO said.

What commuters should expect next

Passenger services on the Pink Line are scheduled to commence on November 4, initially covering 17 of the corridor's 23 stations, with the remaining stations expected to become operational in phases, according to the inauguration coverage. The PMO announcement ahead of the event did not give a completion timetable for Phase-II.

For Pune residents, the immediate change is the Hinjewadi-Shivajinagar link. Whether it cuts the one-to-two-hour road journeys Fadnavis cited will depend on service frequency, last-mile connections from stations, and fares — details that will become clear once passenger operations begin.
